name: Alfama
description: The oldest neighbourhood in Lisbon, surviving the 1755 earthquake. A tangle of medieval lanes climbing from the river to São Jorge castle, full of fado, tile-clad façades, and tiny taverns.

name: Príncipe Real
description: Elegant 19th-century neighbourhood north of Bairro Alto, with concept stores, design hotels, a leafy garden square, and some of the city's best independent restaurants.

name: Marvila
description: Post-industrial eastern district reborn as Lisbon's creative quarter — galleries, breweries, design studios, riverside warehouses. Where much of the contemporary art scene lives.

name: Alcântara
description: Riverside district under the 25 de Abril bridge, home to LX Factory and Unicorn Factory Lisboa — the NFC Summit venue. Mix of industrial heritage and creative reuse.

name: Chiado
description: Lisbon's elegant cultural heart — bookshops, the National Theatre, historic cafés, and a smooth gradient down to the river. Where most first-time visitors land.
